items.title: Stanford Researchers Introduce TRACE: A Capability-Targeted Agentic Training System That Turns Recurrent Agent Failures Into Synthetic RL Environment
items.summary: Stanford researchers developed TRACE, a new agentic training system addressing repeated failures in large language models (LLMs). TRACE diagnoses specific capability gaps by analyzing an agent's failed execution trajectories. It then synthesizes a unique and verifiable Reinforcement Learning (RL) environment for each identified gap. The system trains a dedicated LoRA adapter for every capability, routing tokens across these experts for improvement. Implementation increased τ²-Bench scores by 15.3 points and achieved a 73.2% Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified.
items.audio_script: From MarkTechPost, "Stanford Researchers Introduce TRACE: A Capability-Targeted Agentic Training System That Turns Recurrent Agent Failures Into Synthetic RL Environment." The announcement details a novel training system designed to mitigate persistent failure patterns observed in large language models. This new architecture diagnoses precise functional deficiencies by analyzing an agent's history of failed operations, subsequently constructing a specialized and validated Reinforcement Learning environment for each identified weakness. To facilitate improvement, the system trains discrete LoRA adapters for every capability gap found, routing processing tokens across these expert modules for focused refinement, which resulted in notable performance increases including a 15.3 point rise on τ²-Bench scores and a 73.2% Pass@1 metric on SWE-bench Verified benchmarks. This development signals a substantial methodological advance toward achieving more reliable and modularly improved AI agent performance across complex tasks.

items.title: Prime Intellect Releases Verifiers v1: Composable Tasksets, Harnesses, and Runtimes for Agentic RL Training and Evaluations
items.summary: Prime Intellect released verifiers 0.2.0, previewing a rewritten "v1" core under the `verifiers.v1` namespace. This new structure decomposes an environment into three distinct components: a taskset (defining the goal), a harness (defining the process), and a runtime (defining the execution context). These components are linked by an interception server that manages requests and records traces suitable for training. A key feature is the ability for any taskset to operate under any compatible harness. At launch, the system supports full prime-rl training capabilities.

items.title: RAG vs Fine-Tuning Explained: What They Actually Do and When to Use Each
items.summary: Compares Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and fine-tuning as two distinct approaches for improving large language models. Explains that the choice between them depends on the specific problem, rather than one technique universally outperforming the other. RAG enhances model outputs by retrieving external, up-to-date knowledge before generating a response. Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model's weights to perform better on specific task types or stylistic variations using specialized data. Selecting the right method requires understanding whether the need is for factual grounding (RAG) or behavioral modification (fine-tuning).

items.title: sqlite-utils 4.1.1
items.summary: Version 4.1.1 of `sqlite-utils` primarily addresses an edge case concerning transactions and foreign key constraints. Specifically, `table.transform()` now correctly raises a `TransactionError` when called within a transaction if `PRAGMA foreign_keys` is enabled and the table has destructive `ON DELETE` actions (CASCADE, SET NULL, or SET DEFAULT). This change prevents unintended deletion or modification of referencing rows that could occur because PRAGMA settings cannot be changed mid-transaction. Additionally, the documentation now features cross-referencing links between the CLI and Python API sections for better user navigation.
items.audio_script:
From Simon Willison's Weblog, "sqlite-utils 4.1.1." The latest update addresses a specific edge case related to transactions and foreign key constraints within the SQLite environment. This version modifies the behavior of table transformation when operating under active database transactions that utilize foreign keys with destructive deletion actions like CASCADE or SET NULL.

The core improvement ensures that if PRAGMA foreign_keys is enabled, the library will now correctly raise a TransactionError during calling the transform method inside an existing transaction, preventing unforeseen data loss from potential changes in PRAGMA settings mid-operation. Further enhancements include updated documentation featuring cross-referencing links between the command-line interface and Python API sections to improve user navigation efficiency across both platforms.

This refinement solidifies adherence to SQLite's transactional integrity rules for developers building complex database applications utilizing Python tooling.

items.title: Interval Certifications for Multilayered Perceptrons via Lattice Traversal
items.summary: A new theoretical framework reduces adversarial robustness for multilayered perceptrons to a lattice traversal problem involving input point intervals. Sound certification ensures the MLP's prediction remains unchanged within an interval $I$ containing $\mathbf{x}$, while complete certification guarantees a change in prediction upon leaving $I$. The authors introduce lattice traversal operators applied via a refine & verify iterative scheme, guaranteeing sound maximality and complete minimality using formal verifiers. They find that optimizing for complete certifications is achievable in polynomial oracle calls, unlike the strong intractability proven for sound certifications. Furthermore, logarithmic algorithms are presented for optimization within symmetric intervals, validated by an empirical evaluation using ParallelepipedoNN.

items.title: CogniConsole: Externalizing Inference-Time Control as a Formal Abstraction for Reliable LLM Interactions
items.summary: CogniConsole introduces a method to externalize inference-time control—the computational layer managing task framing and context selection—as a structured interface. This architecture combines programmatic coordination with bounded prompt-based reasoning to govern LLM interactions. Through testing, the research demonstrated that increasing structural scaffolding systematically reduces output variance and failure rates, even when using the same fixed model. The findings suggest that many system failures stem from insufficient control specification rather than inherent limitations in model capability. Consequently, this work establishes inference-time control as a critical, first-class abstraction for designing reliable LLM systems.

items.title: GATS: Graph-Augmented Tree Search with Layered World Models for Efficient Agent Planning
items.summary: GATS introduces a new planning framework combining UCB1-based tree search with a layered world model to improve efficiency over existing methods like LATS and ReAct. This three-layer model integrates symbolic action matching, execution statistics, and limited LLM prediction only when necessary. By eliminating per-step LLM calls during inference, GATS significantly reduces computational cost and stochasticity. On synthetic tasks, it achieved a 100% success rate compared to LATS's 92% and ReAct's 64%. Across a stress test of 12 scenarios, GATS maintained perfect success while other models showed marked performance degradation.

items.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks with Dense Reward-Based Grading
items.summary: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench introduces a new benchmark featuring 46 complex tasks across nine categories, including software engineering and scientific computing. It addresses limitations of existing benchmarks by decomposing tasks into fine-grained subtasks to provide dense intermediate rewards and partial credit. These tasks necessitate significant computational resources, often requiring hundreds of episodes over minutes to hours for completion. Evaluation on this benchmark stresses long-horizon planning, context management, and iterative debugging abilities in frontier AI models. Testing 15 frontier models showed the strongest agent achieved only moderate pass rates at both high partial and perfect reward thresholds.

items.title: A Formalization of the Mean-Field Derivation of the Vlasov Equation: AI-Assisted Lean Formalization as a Strategy Game
items.summary: A formalization of the mean-field derivation for the Vlasov equation was achieved by guiding an AI assistant within the Lean 4 proof assistant, treating the process as a "formalization game." This project successfully formalized well-posedness proofs—including existence, uniqueness, and stability estimates—for the nonlinear Vlasov equation. The mathematician's role involved directing the AI by scoping definitions and handling library gaps rather than writing the proofs directly. A significant outcome was an optimal-transport machinery that compiled as a self-contained, reusable layer against Mathlib alone. These headline theorems were completed in roughly one week, with the entire development taking about a month.

items.title: ARCANA: A Reflective Multi-Agent Program Synthesis Framework for ARC-AGI-2 Reasoning
items.summary: ARCANA is introduced as a collaborative multi-agent framework designed to solve ARC AGI 2 tasks efficiently under strict resource limits. It structures the problem by breaking down each task into sequential phases: perception, hypothesis generation, symbolic execution, and reflective refinement. Agents include one that builds object-centric scene graphs from raw grids, another proposing diverse DSL programs via a latent policy, and a symbolic executor for verification. A final reflective agent synthesizes failure-driven feedback to guide subsequent iterations. These components communicate over a shared differentiable blackboard, orchestrated by a learned meta controller for enhanced reasoning performance.

items.title: Neuro-Agentic Control: A Deep Learning-based LLM-Powered Agentic AI Framework for Controlling Security Controls
items.summary: Cyberattacks on industrial IoT systems reveal shortcomings in traditional rule-based monitoring. To address this, a novel neuro-agentic control framework couples an LLM planner with a Time-Series Foundation Model (TimesFM). This architecture incorporates a "Counterfactual Physics Injection" mechanism to simulate proposed actions before deployment. This simulation allows the system to safely reject unsafe or hallucinatory interventions from the LLM. Evaluations on an industrial dataset showed this framework prevented more breaches and executed zero physically invalid actions compared to baseline models.

items.title: L-MAD: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Debate Structures in Legal Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces the Legal Multi-Agent Debate (L-MAD) framework to systematically evaluate debate structures for Legal Textual Entailment. Assigning distinct expert personas significantly boosts performance over single-agent baselines by up to 8\%. Analysis reveals that increasing agent population reduces inconsistency and improves accuracy in reasoning tasks. However, extending discussion rounds leads to detrimental "over-deliberation drift," causing agents to reinforce errors. Findings establish practical boundaries for deploying multi-agent systems in critical legal reasoning environments.

items.title: MedRealMM: A Real-World Multimodal Benchmark for Chinese Online Medical Consultation
items.summary: Introducing MedRealMM, a large-scale benchmark built from de-identified patient-doctor interactions within Chinese internet hospitals to better evaluate LLMs in online medical consultation. This dataset utilizes a Multimodal Clinical Challenge Point (MCCP) framework to convert authentic consultations into standardized next-response generation tasks while retaining text and image context. Each instance is evaluated using a physician-refined rubric that rewards desirable clinical behaviors and penalizes unsafe responses. The initial release comprises 5,620 real-world multimodal cases across 64 departments, testing both general and specialized LLMs. Evaluation demonstrates that image input is crucial for reliable performance, but models struggle with safety-sensitive error avoidance compared to online physicians.

items.title: KV-PRM: Efficient Process Reward Modeling via KV-Cache Transfer for Multi-Agent Test-Time Scaling
items.summary: Process Reward Models (PRMs) are effective for guiding multi-agent system scaling during testing but suffer from quadratic computational costs due to re-encoding entire trajectories. KV-PRM addresses this by directly utilizing the Key-Value (KV) cache generated during LLM inference instead of reprocessing text. This method reduces the scoring complexity from $O(L^2)$ to linear $O(L)$. Benchmarks across MATH, GSM8K, and AIME show that KV-PRM meets or exceeds text-based PRMs' performance while achieving massive efficiency gains. Specifically, it demonstrates up to a 5,000x reduction in scoring FLOPs and a 34x reduction in memory footprint compared to previous methods.

items.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models via Interactions
items.summary: Research proposes a unified framework to understand knowledge distillation (KD) mechanisms in Large Language Models by decomposing LLM output scores into constituent interactions. By analyzing these interactions, the study reveals that the common underlying mechanism for various KD methods is interaction sparsification, where student models retain only necessary relationships. Furthermore, performance variation among KD techniques correlates with their ability to handle complex interactions effectively. To capitalize on this, a novel plug-and-play loss function called Complex Interaction Penalty (CIP) is introduced. Empirical testing confirms that incorporating CIP consistently enhances the performance of various KD methods across diverse benchmarks.

items.title: iLENS: Interpretable LLM-Guided Mixture-of-Experts for Neuroimaging Survival Analysis
items.summary: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) prediction during its prodromal stage requires accurate survival models that current methods lack in interpretability and reasoning. Introducing iLENS, a framework combines an interpretable Large Language Model (LLM) with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE). This approach utilizes the LLM to synthesize both structured neuroimaging measurements and unstructured data for expert guidance. iLENS achieves competitive predictive performance while offering robust patient subtyping capabilities. Critically, it provides transparent, biologically grounded rationales explaining its decision-making process for clinical support.

items.title: Signed Symmetric Quantization for Few-Bit Integers
items.summary: Standard symmetric quantization's fixed positive scale can cause clipping of positive outliers when using signed integer alphabets. Asymmetric quantization solves this with a zero point but incurs runtime penalties. Signed symmetric quantization offers a third alternative, maintaining symmetric performance while addressing outlier clipping through a principled sign selection rule. Theoretical analysis proves the proposed "signed absmax grid" is conditionally bound-optimal for $\ell_2$ quantization error in many pre-trained LLMs at low bit widths. Empirical testing confirms this method improves perplexity and accuracy compared to standard unsigned quantizers without added inference cost.

items.title: Sticky Routing: Training MoE Models for Memory-Efficient Inference
items.summary: StickyMoE introduces a novel, differentiable routing consistency loss for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models to improve memory efficiency during inference. This loss penalizes abrupt expert switching between adjacent tokens, guiding the router to maintain consistent expert assignments over semantically linked text spans. Unlike existing methods that are either system-level or applied post-training, StickyMoE co-adapts routing decisions from initial training steps without architectural changes. Experiments demonstrate that StickyMoE can reduce the expert switch rate by up to 60% while causing less than 4% perplexity degradation. This suggests that instilling temporal locality directly at training time is highly effective for MoE models.

items.title: Reward Transport: Property Control in Flow Matching via Noise-Space Alignment
items.summary: Introduces Reward Transport, a method treating the flow matching coupling as an interface for structural control rather than just a computational choice. It uses optimal transport during training to align a scalar noise-space coordinate with target molecular properties like $\log P$ or QED. At inference, varying this single coordinate steers the generated distribution without needing external models or complex gradient calculations. This principled approach achieves continuous, tunable control over generation characteristics by modifying only this alignment parameter. Experiments show that manipulating this knob can induce opposite structural changes for different targets, indicating specific property control rather than generalized size bias.

items.title: Director: Accelerating Distributed MoE Serving via Online Proactive Expert Placement
items.summary: Director is a novel distributed system designed to minimize the end-to-end serving latency of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models through online, proactive expert placement. It addresses limitations in previous methods by predicting incoming requests' expert activation patterns using lightweight cascaded predictors or quantized replicas. The system handles dynamic changes and migration costs via an online module that performs transfers during compute-bound phases to minimize downtime. At its core, Director utilizes a relaxation-based optimizer operating under capacity constraints, achieving a $(1+\epsilon)$ approximation ratio in polynomial time. Experiments demonstrate significant latency reductions of $11\%$ to $55\%$ across popular MoE models like Mistral and Qwen.

items.title: LieBN: Batch Normalization over Lie Groups
items.summary: Manifold-valued measurements are common in machine learning, necessitating specific normalization techniques for deep neural networks operating on curved spaces. Existing Riemannian normalization methods are often limited to specific geometries or fail to normalize sample distributions effectively across different manifolds. The proposed LieBN framework offers a solution by providing general Riemannian Batch Normalization (RBN) over the structure of Lie groups. It utilizes theoretically convenient left- and right-invariant metrics inherent to all Lie groups, ensuring control over both the Riemannian mean and variance. Validation confirms LieBN's effectiveness across nine distinct geometries, including the SPD manifold and rotation matrix group.

items.title: HERO: A Heterogeneity-Aware Benchmark Library for Federated Continual Learning
items.summary: Federated continual learning (FCL) evaluations are currently difficult to compare due to simultaneous changes in datasets, task splits, and client data divisions. HERO introduces a heterogeneity-aware benchmark library specifically designed for FCL comparison. It systematically separates the choices of task split, client data split, and client task sequence into comparable benchmark streams. The core benchmark utilizes parameters ($\alpha$ and $\rho$) to control client data skew and task-order mismatch, respectively. Evaluation on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet demonstrates that performance varies significantly across different learning settings, highlighting the need for reproducible benchmarks like HERO.

items.title: DaDaDa: A Dataset for Data Pricing in Data Marketplaces
items.summary: Determining accurate prices for data products in growing data marketplaces is challenging because traditional economic models are insufficient. While the sales comparison approach offers promise, it lacks standardized pricing benchmarks across various platforms. To address this gap, researchers introduce \texttt{DaDaDa}, a novel dataset containing metadata for 16,147 data products sourced from nine major global marketplaces. This resource allows for the training of predictive models to establish necessary price benchmarks for new data offerings. Furthermore, \texttt{DaDaDa} supports secondary applications, including data product classification and retrieval, with supporting code also released online.

items.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
items.summary: High LLM inference costs necessitate acceleration via weight matrix sparsity, but current GPUs struggle with moderate unstructured sparsity levels ($\sim 50\%$). This paper introduces an efficient GPU method for LLMs with such sparsity using a novel three-layer storage format. The format includes a Sparse-TC layer utilizing sparse tensor cores, a Slot-Filling layer for compression, and a Residual Layer for accurate computation. A jointly designed SpMM kernel leverages both sparse tensor cores and CUDA cores to create an optimized execution pipeline. Evaluations demonstrate that this method achieves the first instance of outperforming dense multiplication on modern HBM-equipped GPUs, yielding up to 1.64x kernel speedup over prior state-of-the-art methods.

items.title: EHR-MPC: Inference-Time Control for Sepsis Treatment with Generative Patient Digital Twins
items.summary: Sepsis mortality rates are high, but optimal treatment strategies are debated, and current reinforcement learning methods lack adaptability during care. Introducing EHRMPC, the proposed framework separates patient dynamics learning from treatment optimization. It utilizes a generative electronic health record (EHR) model to create a predictive "digital twin" of the patient. This digital twin allows for model predictive control (MPC) by simulating treatment outcomes at inference time for optimal planning. Evaluation across an 8-hospital ICU sepsis cohort showed EHRMPC achieved comparable off-policy performance and improved simulation results compared to existing RL baselines.

items.title: Influence Diagnostics in High-dimensional M-estimation: Precise Asymptotics
items.summary: Leave-one-out influence classically measures how much removing a single training point affects model accuracy. Analyzing these influences becomes complex in high dimensions because sample effects depend non-trivially on all other data points. For convex M-estimation under Gaussian design, the study characterizes the limiting distribution of these influences when $n$ and $d$ are both large ($n\asymp d$). This characterization shows that influential samples are likely situated near the decision boundary. Consequently, this finding supports using proximity to the boundary as a selection heuristic in active learning tasks.

items.title: Spectrally Deconfounded Gradient Boosting
items.summary: Machine learning methods can erroneously learn associations from unobserved confounders; spectral deconfounding addresses this by shrinking high-variance directions in the covariate matrix containing latent information. This research develops a novel, nonlinear spectral deconfounding framework specifically for gradient boosting. The approach substitutes the standard squared-error loss with a specialized spectral loss that dampens learning along confounding directions. Deconfounding effectiveness requires the interplay between spectral shrinkage and regularization, particularly during early stopping. Experiments show this spectrally deconfounded boosting improves target function estimation under hidden confounders while maintaining scalability.

items.title: Deep Gaussian Processes on Directed Acyclic Graphs
items.summary: Models representing real-world processes as compositions along Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) face challenges due to partially observed, noisy, and heterogeneously sampled measurements. To address this, Deep Gaussian Processes over DAGs are introduced by placing priors directly over the underlying functions. Research theoretically analyzes prior-collapse behavior, detailing how graph topology and intermediate data affect information preservation. The authors develop a structured variational approximation that maintains graph dependencies and captures "explaining-away" effects at collider nodes. Empirical testing validates the methodology across various complex systems, achieving state-of-the-art performance while providing interpretability.

items.title: Adaptive Bayes exactly tracks information over intrinsic time
items.summary: Bayesian and multiplicative-weights updates for expert reweighting exhibit an exact information-accounting identity regarding cumulative regret. On any given round, the excess loss compared to a comparator equals an immediate payment reflecting exposed uncertainty plus a decrease in information distance from the current weights to that comparator. Summing these one-step balances yields two exact adaptive decompositions of cumulative regret. These exact decompositions show that favorable stochastic regimes manifest as self-bounding properties of the realized "intrinsic time." This pathwise account applies uniformly across methods like Hedge, contextual bandits, and online convex optimization.

items.title: A Statistical Test for the Benefits of Personalizing Interventions
items.summary: A new statistical hypothesis test evaluates whether personalized interventions outperform deploying the single best available intervention, using historical data. The method maintains strict control over type-I errors while achieving asymptotic normality with minimal variance under specific conditions. This tool supports decision-makers across various fields, including medicine, marketing, and education. Its versatility is demonstrated through successful results on diverse datasets covering job training, depression treatment, and recommendation systems. Ultimately, it provides a simple yet powerful way to quantify the potential advantages of personalized approaches.

items.title: Nonconvex Composite Functional Constraints via First-Order Augmented Lagrangian Methods under Local Regularity
items.summary: Investigates the nonasymptotic convergence of primal-dual methods for nonconvex constrained optimization problems with a convex-composite structure. The method addresses complications from constraint violation and unbounded multipliers by restricting the dual variable to an auxiliary compact set. It analyzes a smoothed prox-linear augmented Lagrangian via a nonsmooth nonconvex-concave minimax reformulation. A key contribution is showing how stationarity of a truncated minimax problem yields a KKT certificate for the original problem. Convergence rates are established, achieving $O(K^{-1/3})$ with dual regularization and potentially a sharper $O(K^{-1/2})$ rate under specific structural assumptions.

items.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Partially Observed Actions
items.summary: Addresses the stochastic linear bandit with partially observed actions, common in fields like recommendations where full action information is unavailable. While general settings preclude sublinear regret, the authors demonstrate overcoming this barrier when action vectors possess low intrinsic dimension. A proposed algorithm, TOFU-POV, estimates the latent action subspace from masked observations and then applies OFUL in these reduced coordinates. Theoretically, TOFU-POV achieves $\sqrt{T}$ regret scaling with the intrinsic dimension, not the ambient dimension. The work also introduces a rank-adaptive alternative and provides novel lower bounds validating its performance.

items.title: Optimal Top-$k$ Identification from Pairwise Comparisons
items.summary: Addresses the active learning challenge of identifying the top-$k$ items from noisy pairwise comparisons with a fixed error probability $\delta$. The goal is to minimize the expected number of required comparisons (sample complexity). Previous research has established asymptotic optimality for many pure exploration problems, but not for top-$k$ identification via pairwise comparisons under latent utility models. Novel work characterizes the lower bound using a saddle-point formulation, leading to an efficient primal-dual procedure. This enables constructing and proving an adaptive comparison-allocation algorithm that achieves asymptotic optimality in this setting.
